newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's six-month bill yields expected stable.
newsitem.headline: Spain's six-month bill yields expected stable.

text.p: After a steady decline in recent months, the yield on Spanish six-month Treasury bills could remain stable or show a slight upturn at Wednesday's auction, dealers said on Tuesday.
The yield is likely to be between 5.34 percent and 5.40, not far from 5.342 percent, its record low set on January 15 and then repeated on January 29.
But dealers added recent tensions in money market rates should soon be over as the peseta seems to have found relative stability.
They said one-year bills, whose yield rose to 5.172 percent from 5.052 percent at an auction last Wednesday, are now trading at lower levels in the secondary market.
"Tomorrow's auction is attracting little interest, but we expect a marginal yield around the same levels we saw two weeks ago," a dealer in Madrid said.
"We're seeing buying interest in one-year bills and if things go smoothly the lower trend in yields could re-start," he said.
